collection_summary:
Original `causal` instance filling one of the remaining gap-4 categories (causal). NEW **Science/Conservation** subdomain. NEW entity class: extinct animal taxa (no other instance is keyed by an animal common name). Natural human query: 'Which animals have gone extinct since 1900, and what was the primary cause for each?'

Multi-wiki source plan (24 URLs): Wikipedia 'List of recently extinct mammals' + 'List of bird extinctions by year' as master articles supplying the broad taxonomic universe + year ordering; 22 per-taxon Wikipedia articles grounding Continent + Primary Causes for each row. Per-taxon articles are load-bearing for row-level cause and continent grounding because the master articles do not uniformly state continent of origin or full primary-cause lists.

Result: 22 rows × 5 columns (Common Name PK, Scientific Name, Continent of Origin, Year of Last Confirmed Record [text, source-faithful], Primary Causes [text, semicolon-delimited]), 0 duplicates. Taxa universe: 12 full species + 6 subspecies + 4 regional/local-form populations (Bali/Caspian/Javan tigers + Barbary lion — current Wikipedia taxonomy classes these as populations of broader subspecies rather than independent subspecies). 21 of 22 rows multi-cause; 1 single-cause (Bubal hartebeest). 21 specific-year rows + 1 decade-only row (Bali tiger 'late 1930s' — article gives no single year for the last record).

Cycle-2 audit fixes (3 BLOCKING + 2 HYG + 1 SUGGESTION-deferred): B1 Year relation pivot to 'last confirmed sighting (wild or captive, whichever later)' per per-taxon Wikipedia articles, replacing the unsupported 'declared extinct' / decade-form values from cycle-1 (Caspian tiger '1970s' → 1970, Javan tiger '1980s' → 1976, Bali tiger '1950s' → 'late 1930s', Barbary lion '1960s' → 1942, Japanese sea lion '1970s' → 1974, plus rebases of 7 specific-year rows to wild-or-captive-latest record per article); B2 all 22 cause cells re-grounded against per-taxon Wikipedia articles (Caribbean monk seal 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Overhunting; Overfishing', Japanese wolf 'Hunting' → 'Disease; Persecution; Habitat loss', Heath hen 'Habitat destruction' → 'Hunting; Habitat loss; Inbreeding; Disease', etc. — full row-by-row trace in audit_response.cycle_2.row_changes); B3 row universe reframed as 'taxa (species, subspecies, and regional populations)' since 4 tiger/lion rows are populations not subspecies per current Wikipedia taxonomy; H1 cycle-0/cycle-1 active-state narrative residue (Species PK, source_defined, 2-URL plan, decade-form Year, 8-vs-10 cause count) scrubbed from active fields and preserved only in audit_response history; H2 source_coverage_notes tightened to honestly attribute Continent + Causes to per-taxon articles, not master articles.

Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + cycle-2-extinctions lessons applied: (a) single PK on Common Name; (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via 2 master + 22 per-taxon articles; (c) Year relation explicit and uniform ('last confirmed record per per-taxon article, wild or captive whichever later'); (d) Year filter '≥ 1900 strict on last confirmed record'; (e) Boundary-Aware Fields pattern for multi-cause Primary Causes; (f) honest scope framing 'taxa and populations' rather than 'species' or 'species+subspecies'; (g) deterministic continent rule (continental affinity for islands).
source_coverage_notes:
Twenty-four Wikipedia source URLs combine. Master articles define the broad taxonomic universe (post-1500 extinct mammals + birds); per-taxon articles ground Continent + Primary Causes + Last-Confirmed-Record year for each staged row. Per cycle-2 audit fix H2, this note no longer claims the master articles tabulate every staged tuple — the bird master article especially does not state continent of origin or full primary-cause lists per entry, so per-taxon articles are load-bearing for Continent + Causes.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_recently_extinct_mammals): universe (14 mammal taxa). Confirms the post-1500 extinct-mammals universe and gives year-range context; per-taxon articles supply authoritative row-level Year + Continent + Cause values.
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bird_extinctions_by_year): universe (8 bird taxa). Confirms the post-1500 extinct-birds universe; per-taxon articles supply authoritative row-level grounding.

Per-taxon Wikipedia articles (load-bearing for Continent + Primary Causes + Year):
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_wolf): entity-detail — last confirmed record 1905 (Washikaguchi specimen, Honshu Nara Prefecture). Causes: disease (rabies + canine distemper) + Meiji-era persecution + habitat loss / deforestation.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarpan): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1909 (Russian-empire zoo captive; body text authority over lead's '1918'). Causes: overhunting for meat + habitat-loss range reduction + persecution for damage to hay/pastures.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passenger_pigeon): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1914 (Martha, Cincinnati Zoo captive). Causes: overhunting (commercial-scale) + habitat loss / deforestation.
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_parakeet): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1918 (Incas, Cincinnati Zoo captive). Causes: habitat loss (deforestation) + hunting (feathers + crop-protection) + disease (Snyder's poultry-disease hypothesis as terminal cause).
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubal_hartebeest): entity-detail — last confirmed record 1925 (Missour, Morocco wild kill). Causes: overhunting (colonial-military massacre + sportsmen).
- source_urls[7] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_hen): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1932 (Booming Ben, Martha's Vineyard). Causes: hunting + habitat loss + 1916 fire / inbreeding (sex-ratio skew) + disease + predation.
- source_urls[8] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawai%CA%BBi_%CA%BB%C5%8D%CA%BB%C5%8D): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1934 (Mauna Loa, Hawaii). Causes: mosquito-borne disease + deforestation + hunting (musket-enabled feather collection).
- source_urls[9] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thylacine): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1936 (Hobart Zoo captive). Causes: hunting / bounty hunting + disease (distemper-like) + habitat erosion + invasive species (dingoes).
- source_urls[10] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toolache_wallaby): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 1939 (last captive; wild last sighting 1924). Causes: habitat loss (swamp clearing) + invasive species (European red fox) + hunting (sport + pelt).
- source_urls[11] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laysan_rail): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1944 (Eastern Island, Midway). Causes: habitat loss (rabbit grazing on Laysan) + invasive species (rats on Midway).
- source_urls[12] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Island_rail): entity-detail — last confirmed record 1939 (last museum specimen; cycle-3 audit fix: previously staged 1945 was the WWII extinction-event closure year, not a verified individual record — under the 'latest verified record' rule, the 1939 museum specimen is the authoritative last record. The article frames the WWII 1942-1945 hunting-to-extinction window but does not document individual sightings within it). Causes: overhunting (starving Japanese troops) + habitat loss (aerial bombardment).
- source_urls[13] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bali_tiger): entity-detail — last confirmed record 'late 1930s' (article gives no single year; lead's 'extinct since the 1950s' downgraded by body text). Causes: hunting (Dutch colonial sport hunters) + habitat loss (palm + rice agriculture conversion).
- source_urls[14] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_monk_seal): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1952 (Serranilla Bank). Causes: overhunting (blubber oil + meat) + overfishing (prey collapse). Article explicitly rejects habitat-loss framing.
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbary_lion): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1956 (last known Algerian sighting; cycle-3 audit fix: previously staged 1942 was the last recorded shooting in the Moroccan Atlas, but the article also documents a later 1956 sighting in Algeria. Under the 'latest verified record' rule, 1956 wins over the 1942 kill). Article also notes possible relict survival to mid-1960s as unverified. Causes: hunting (firearms-enabled extermination) + bounty hunting / persecution.
- source_urls[16] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspian_tiger): entity-detail — last confirmed record 1970 (Uludere, Turkey skins; infobox 'Extinct (1970)'). Causes: hunting (military + sportsmen) + prey decline (wild boar / deer overhunting + disease) + habitat loss (cotton-agriculture deforestation).
- source_urls[17] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_sea_lion): entity-detail — last confirmed record 1974 (Rebun Island juvenile specimen). Causes: overhunting (commercial fishery, 16,500-animal harvest) + habitat loss (WWII submarine warfare).
- source_urls[18] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javan_tiger): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1976 (Meru Betiri; declared extinct 2008). Causes: habitat loss (rice-field conversion 1830s+) + hunting / bounty hunting + prey decline (Javan rusa disease loss).
- source_urls[19] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atitl%C3%A1n_grebe): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 1989 (last two birds, Lake Atitlán). Causes: invasive species (smallmouth + largemouth bass introduction 1958-1960 reduced prey + killed chicks) + habitat loss (1976 earthquake lake-level drop) + hybridization (with pied-billed grebe).
- source_urls[20] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenean_ibex): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 2000 (Celia, found dead 6 Jan 2000). Causes: hunting / poaching + competition (with domestic + wild ungulates) + disease.
- source_urls[21] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Po%CA%BBouli): entity-detail — last confirmed individual 2004 (captive male, Maui Bird Conservation Center; only individual extant by 2004). Causes: habitat loss (human activity) + disease (avian malaria, mosquito-borne) + invasive species (Indian axis deer, feral pigs, rats, cats, mongoose) + prey decline (native tree snails).
- source_urls[22] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_black_rhinoceros): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 2006 (Cameroon Northern Province; declared extinct 2011). Causes: poaching (for horn / TCM) + hunting (farmers defending crops).
- source_urls[23] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bramble_Cay_melomys): entity-detail — last confirmed sighting 2009 (Bramble Cay, Torres Strait; declared extinct by Queensland 2016, by Australia 2019). Causes: climate change (sea-level rise / inundation 'root cause') + habitat loss (vegetation/cay erosion as mechanism).

Universe-size sanity: 22 staged rows = 12 full species + 6 subspecies + 4 regional populations; all post-1900 by Year of Last Confirmed Record (1905-2009). The 22 taxa are a curator-selected subset of the well-documented post-1900 extinctions in the 2 master articles (full lists contain ~45+ mammals + ~12 birds); subset focuses on widely-cited / commonsense-knowable taxa across years and continents. Continent distribution: Africa 3, Asia 5, Europe 2, North America 5, Oceania 7. Oceania count is high because many post-1900 extinctions occurred on islands (Hawaii, Tasmania, Australia, Bramble Cay) with high endemic-species + invasive-predator pressure. Cycle-2 audit-flagged stronger bird-side master source 'List of extinct bird species since 1500' (richer per-bird narrative) deferred as SUGGESTION — current 2-master + 22-per-taxon plan already grounds every staged row, and adding the third master would not change row universe or column values.
normalization_decisions: Common Name values use Wikipedia article-title common-name forms ('Thylacine' not 'Tasmanian tiger'; 'Carolina parakeet' lowercase per article style; 'Hawaiian ʻōʻō' preserves Hawaiian diacritics; 'Poʻouli' preserves Hawaiian glottal stop). Scientific Name values use binomial or trinomial Latin form per Wikipedia infobox (e.g., 'Thylacinus cynocephalus'; 'Panthera tigris sondaica' for Bali tiger Bali-population; 'Panthera tigris tigris' for Caspian tiger). Continent of Origin uses standard 6-continent classification with continental-affinity rule for islands ('Africa', 'Asia', 'Europe', 'North America', 'Oceania' represented; Antarctica + South America naturally absent from staged subset). Year of Last Confirmed Record is TEXT, with the rule: 'year of the latest verified record per the per-taxon Wikipedia article — wild sighting, captive individual, or specimen collection, whichever is most recent'. Where the article gives a range (e.g., 'late 1930s' for Bali tiger), the staged value uses the article's stated form. Otherwise specific 4-digit year. 21 of 22 rows have specific years; 1 has 'late 1930s'. Sort order uses parsed leading 4-digit year ('late 1930s' sorts as 1937), then Common Name ASC. Primary Causes is text with semicolon-delimited list format (delimiter '; '). Vocabulary (13 distinct values per cycle-2 audit re-grounding): 'Hunting', 'Overhunting', 'Poaching', 'Overfishing', 'Habitat loss', 'Disease', 'Invasive species', 'Climate change', 'Persecution', 'Prey decline', 'Inbreeding', 'Competition', 'Hybridization'. 21 of 22 rows multi-cause; 1 single-cause (Bubal hartebeest 'Overhunting' — article frames as sole cause). Multi-cause ordering follows the per-taxon Wikipedia article's emphasis: article-foregrounded primary driver first, then contributing factors in narrative order (Caribbean monk seal 'Overhunting; Overfishing' — article foregrounds overhunting first; Bramble Cay melomys 'Climate change; Habitat loss' — article calls climate change the 'root cause' and habitat loss the mechanism).
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with documented risks around (a) multi-cause cells, (b) Year relation, (c) Continent rule for island species. All three resolved via cycle-1 + cycle-2 commitments below.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses extinct animals directly.
- Category: causal (primary, cause-effect relation between taxon and extinction cause(s)) + multi_attribute_projection (secondary, 4 non-key attributes).
- Source plan (post-cycle-2): 2 master + 22 per-taxon Wikipedia articles = 24 URLs. Per-taxon articles are load-bearing for Continent + Causes + Year. (Stronger bird-side master 'List of extinct bird species since 1500' deferred as cycle-2 SUGGESTION.)
- Expected shape: 22 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Common Name.
- Domain: Science/Conservation (new subdomain in Science family).
- Decision: STAGE.

Committed rules (post-cycle-2):
1) Primary Causes as semicolon-delimited list (Boundary-Aware Fields pattern). Delimiter '; '. Title-case cause names. 13 distinct vocabulary values per per-taxon-article re-grounding (cycle-2): 'Hunting', 'Overhunting', 'Poaching', 'Overfishing', 'Habitat loss', 'Disease', 'Invasive species', 'Climate change', 'Persecution', 'Prey decline', 'Inbreeding', 'Competition', 'Hybridization'.
2) Cause vocabulary preserves per-taxon-article word choice: 'Hunting' vs 'Overhunting' (overhunting = article emphasizes commercial-scale or population-collapse-scale hunting); 'Hunting' vs 'Poaching' (poaching = illegal/protected-status killing, e.g., Western black rhino); 'Hunting' vs 'Persecution' (persecution = bounty/extermination policy, e.g., Japanese wolf Meiji-era persecution, Tarpan damage-to-hay-stores persecution). 'Habitat loss' subsumes article variants ('habitat destruction', 'habitat degradation', 'deforestation') — cycle-2 consolidated for clarity vs the cycle-1 nuance-split.
3) Year of Last Confirmed Record relation = 'year of the latest verified record per the per-taxon Wikipedia article — wild sighting, captive individual, or specimen collection, whichever is most recent'. This is the cycle-2 audit-driven pivot from the earlier 'declared extinct' relation. Applies uniformly: where wild and captive last records both exist, use the later (Tarpan captive 1909 over wild 1879; Passenger pigeon captive 1914 over wild 1902; Thylacine captive 1936 over wild 1930; Toolache wallaby captive 1939 over wild 1924; Carolina parakeet captive 1918 over wild 1904). Where only wild records exist, use that (Japanese wolf 1905, Bubal hartebeest 1925, Caribbean monk seal 1952, etc.). Where only captive records exist, use that (Poʻouli 2004 last captive male). Where the article gives a range with no individual record within it (Wake Island rail '1942-1945' WWII extinction-event window) and a verified earlier record exists, use the earlier verified record (Wake Island rail 1939 last museum specimen — cycle-3 audit fix: previously 1945 end-bound, corrected under the 'verified record' clause of the rule). Where the article gives a range without specific individuals (Bali tiger 'late 1930s'), keep the article's stated form verbatim. For Barbary lion: 1956 last sighting (Algeria) wins over the earlier 1942 shooting kill (Moroccan Atlas) under the 'latest verified record' rule — cycle-3 audit fix.
4) Year filter '≥ 1900 strict on last confirmed record': Steller's sea cow (1768), Falkland Islands wolf (1876), Sea mink (1894), Quagga (1883) and other pre-1900 famous extinctions excluded. Tarpan body-text last-captive 1909 keeps it post-1900 (vs lead's 1918 ambiguity or body's wild-only 1879).
5) Continent of Origin = continental affinity rule (islands attributed to nearest continent: Caribbean→North America, Hawaii/Pacific→Oceania, Tasmania/Australian islands→Oceania, Madagascar→Africa, Bramble Cay→Oceania).
6) Common Name PK (English): Wikipedia article-title common-name forms; scientific name in separate non-key column.
7) Universe = 22-taxon curator subset of master articles' full extinction lists (~57+ post-1900 mammals + birds). Subset focuses on widely-cited / commonsense-knowable taxa across years and continents; less-famous rodents and small mammals excluded for LLM-knowability. claim_type 'partially_supplemented' honestly reflects the curator-subset selection (see proposed_supplements field).
8) Taxa+populations framing: 12 full species + 6 subspecies + 4 regional populations (Bali / Caspian / Javan tigers + Barbary lion — current Wikipedia taxonomy classes these as populations of broader subspecies P. t. sondaica / P. t. tigris / P. l. leo rather than independent subspecies). Cycle-2 audit fix B3 reframed title from 'animal taxa (species and subspecies)' to 'animal taxa (species, subspecies, and regional populations)'.
9) operation_type 'join' (logical taxon ⋈ causes join via the multi-cause attribution).

Cycle-1 history (closed): 4 BLOCKING + 1 HYG addressed — claim_type pivot to partially_supplemented; +22 per-taxon URLs; Year column TEXT with then-source-exact form; column rename Species → Common Name; cause-count narrative fix 8 → 10. (See audit_response.cycle_1.)

Cycle-2 history (closed): 3 BLOCKING + 2 HYG addressed — Year relation pivot to last confirmed sighting with all 22 row values rebased against per-taxon articles; all 22 Primary Causes cells re-grounded against per-taxon articles (Caribbean monk seal 'Overhunting; Overfishing', Japanese wolf 'Disease; Persecution; Habitat loss', etc.); taxa+populations framing; cycle-0/cycle-1 active-narrative residue scrubbed; source_coverage_notes tightened. (See audit_response.cycle_2 for per-row change trace.)
open_questions: 1) Universe is curator-supplemented subset of the master articles' full extinction lists (22 of ~57+ post-1900 taxa). Selection emphasizes widely-cited / commonsense-knowable taxa; less-famous rodents and small mammals are excluded for LLM-knowability. Claim_type 'partially_supplemented' with explicit subset disclosure in proposed_supplements. 2) Cause vocabulary re-grounded against per-taxon articles (cycle-2). Some single-cause article framings (e.g., Bubal hartebeest 'Overhunting' as sole cause) reflect article emphasis; an LLM under test could defensibly name 1-2 additional contributing causes. Multi-cause ordering follows article narrative emphasis. 3) Year of Last Confirmed Record uses 'wild-or-captive-latest' rule per per-taxon article. An LLM naming a sub-rule year (wild-only, IUCN-declared, official-declaration) for a row where the rule gives a different value should be considered under the staged rule. Specific candidates with rule-sensitive answers: Tarpan (1879 wild / 1909 captive, staged 1909); Passenger pigeon (1902 wild / 1914 captive Martha, staged 1914); Thylacine (1930 wild / 1936 captive Hobart, staged 1936); Toolache wallaby (1924 wild / 1939 captive, staged 1939); Western black rhino (2006 sighting / 2011 IUCN-declared, staged 2006); Bramble Cay melomys (2009 sighting / 2016 Queensland-declared / 2019 Australia-declared, staged 2009). 4) Continent for island species uses continental-affinity (Hawaii→Oceania, Caribbean→North America, Bramble Cay→Oceania). An LLM under test placing Hawaii under 'North America' (US-state reading) or Caribbean monk seal under 'Central America' could be partially credited as defensible alternative readings. 5) Year-filter '≥ 1900 strict on last confirmed record': Steller's sea cow (1768), Falkland Islands wolf (1876), Sea mink (1894), Quagga (1883) excluded. An LLM including them would miss the filter. 6) Bali tiger 'late 1930s' is the only non-specific-year row (article gives no single year for the last record). An LLM responding with a specific year like 1937 or 1939 should be partially credited as the article-implied range. 7) Western black rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis longipes) is a subspecies declared extinct 2011 by IUCN; the species black rhinoceros survives via other subspecies. Staged year is 2006 (last sighting), not 2011 (declaration). 8) Bramble Cay melomys (2016) is the article-foregrounded 'first mammalian climate-change extinction'; staged year is 2009 (last sighting), not 2016 (Queensland declaration) or 2019 (Australia declaration). 9) Cycle-2 audit-flagged SUGGESTION to add 'List of extinct bird species since 1500' as a stronger bird-side master was deferred — current 2-master + 22-per-taxon plan already grounds every staged row, and adding the third master would not change row universe or column values. 10) Taxa+populations framing: 4 tiger/lion rows (Bali, Caspian, Javan, Barbary) are regional populations of broader subspecies per current Wikipedia taxonomy. An LLM categorizing them strictly as 'subspecies' should be considered under the staged 'taxa and populations' rubric.
proposed_supplements: The 22-row staged universe is a curator-supplemented subset of the 2 master Wikipedia articles' full extinction lists (~57+ post-1900 mammals + birds combined). Selected 22 widely-cited / commonsense-knowable taxa; excluded ~35 less-famous post-1900 extinctions (Lesser bilby 1960s, Desert bandicoot 1943, Crescent nail-tail wallaby 1956, Galápagos mice species, Christmas Island shrew, various flying foxes, etc.) for LLM-knowability. Per-taxon supplementation: each staged row's Year + Continent + Cause is grounded by both (a) the master article for the taxonomic class and (b) the per-taxon Wikipedia article (24 URLs total). The curator subset is partially_supplemented in the row-selection sense: the named-taxa universe (all post-1900 extinctions in the master articles) is source-defined, but the within-universe 22-taxon selection is curator-supplemented for LLM-knowability.

blocking_addressed: B1 (claim_type source_defined overstated): the 22 staged rows are a curator subset of the master articles' ~57+ post-1900 extinction lists. Cycle-1 fix: changed claim_type 'source_defined' → 'partially_supplemented' + added proposed_supplements field documenting the curator-subset audit trail.

B2 (master URLs don't support Primary Causes + Continent uniformly): cycle-0 source_urls = 2 master articles only. Cycle-1 fix: added 22 per-taxon Wikipedia URLs (one per staged row) to source_urls — source_count 2 → 24.

B3 (Year not source-faithful, non-uniform scalarization): cycle-0 had numeric scalar Year values for decade-only source entries. Cycle-1 fix: Year column changed numeric → TEXT with then-source-exact form (5 decade rows + 17 specific-year rows). (Note: cycle-2 audit later flagged that the cycle-1 decade values themselves didn't match per-taxon articles — see cycle_2.B1.)

B4 (schema/title says Species but table includes subspecies): cycle-0 PK column was 'Species'. Cycle-1 fix: PK column renamed 'Species' → 'Common Name'; title reframed to 'animal taxa (species and subspecies)'.
hygiene_addressed: H1 (cause vocabulary count mismatch): cycle-0 decision_log + _extraction_notes said '8 distinct cause values' but CSV had 10. Cycle-1 fix: corrected count 8 → 10.

blocking_addressed: B1 (Year relation under-specified, per-taxon-article values conflict with cycle-1 decade staging): cycle-1's source-exact decade-form values (Caspian '1970s', Javan '1980s', Bali '1950s', Barbary '1960s', Japanese sea lion '1970s') didn't match the per-taxon Wikipedia articles, which give specific years or different decades. Cycle-2 fix: column renamed 'Year Declared Extinct' → 'Year of Last Confirmed Record'; rule committed as 'year of the latest verified record per the per-taxon Wikipedia article — wild sighting, captive individual, or specimen collection, whichever is most recent'. All 22 row values rebased: Caspian tiger 1970s → 1970 (Uludere Turkey skins; infobox 'Extinct (1970)'); Javan tiger 1980s → 1976 (Meru Betiri last sighting); Bali tiger 1950s → 'late 1930s' (article's stated form, no single year); Barbary lion 1960s → 1942 (Tizi n'Tichka shooting); Japanese sea lion 1970s → 1974 (Rebun juvenile). Specific-year rebases: Tarpan 1909 (kept, body-text captive); Passenger pigeon 1914→1914 (kept, Martha); Carolina parakeet 1918→1918 (kept, Incas); Japanese wolf 1905→1905 (kept, Washikaguchi); Thylacine 1936→1936 (kept, Hobart); Toolache wallaby 1939→1939 (kept, last captive); Heath hen 1932→1932 (kept, Booming Ben); Hawaiian ʻōʻō 1934→1934 (kept, Mauna Loa); Bubal hartebeest 1925→1925 (kept, Missour); Laysan rail 1944→1944 (kept, Midway); Wake Island rail 1945→1945 (kept, WWII end); Caribbean monk seal 1952→1952 (kept, Serranilla Bank); Atitlán grebe 1989→1989 (kept); Pyrenean ibex 2000→2000 (kept, Celia); Poʻouli 2004→2004 (kept, captive male); Western black rhinoceros 2011→2006 (changed: 2011 was IUCN-declared year, 2006 is last sighting per article); Bramble Cay melomys 2016→2009 (changed: 2016 was Queensland declaration, 2009 is last sighting per article). Column type stays text to accommodate 'late 1930s'.

B2 (Primary Causes cells not all source-faithful, controlled cause-normalization not documented): cycle-1 cause cells reflected master-article phrasing which the per-taxon articles often contradict. Cycle-2 fix: re-grounded all 22 cause cells against per-taxon Wikipedia articles. Major changes: Caribbean monk seal 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Overhunting; Overfishing' (article explicitly identifies overhunting + overfishing of prey, NOT habitat loss); Japanese wolf 'Hunting' → 'Disease; Persecution; Habitat loss' (article foregrounds rabies + canine distemper first, then Meiji persecution, then deforestation); Heath hen 'Habitat destruction' → 'Hunting; Habitat loss; Inbreeding; Disease' (article emphasizes hunting + 1916 fire + inbreeding sex-ratio skew); Hawaiian ʻōʻō 'Disease; Habitat loss' → 'Disease; Habitat loss; Hunting' (article also names musket-enabled hunting); Thylacine 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Hunting; Disease; Habitat loss; Invasive species' (article also names distemper-like disease + dingo competition); Toolache wallaby 'Hunting; Habitat degradation' → 'Habitat loss; Invasive species; Hunting' (article foregrounds habitat clearing first, then red fox predation); Wake Island rail 'Human disturbance' → 'Overhunting; Habitat loss' (article explicitly names starving Japanese troop hunting + bombardment); Barbary lion 'Hunting' → 'Hunting; Persecution' (article names bounty-driven extermination as separate factor); Caspian tiger 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Hunting; Prey decline; Habitat loss' (article names wild boar/deer prey decimation as separate factor); Atitlán grebe 'Habitat degradation' → 'Invasive species; Habitat loss; Hybridization' (article foregrounds bass introduction first, then earthquake-driven lake drop, then grebe hybridization); Pyrenean ibex 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Hunting; Competition; Disease' (article hedges; lists hunting + ungulate competition + disease, not habitat); Poʻouli 'Disease; Habitat loss' → 'Habitat loss; Disease; Invasive species; Prey decline' (article names mosquito-malaria + 4 invasive predators + native-snail prey decline); Western black rhinoceros 'Poaching' → 'Poaching; Hunting' (article names farmers-defending-crops as separate factor); Tarpan 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Overhunting; Habitat loss; Persecution' (article distinguishes hunting-for-meat from persecution-for-damage); Carolina parakeet 'Hunting; Habitat loss' → 'Habitat loss; Hunting; Disease' (article foregrounds deforestation first, then hunting, then Snyder disease hypothesis); Passenger pigeon 'Overhunting' → 'Overhunting; Habitat loss' (article names deforestation as secondary). Single-cause rows: Bubal hartebeest 'Overhunting' (kept; article frames as sole cause). Vocabulary expanded with article-faithful labels: Persecution, Prey decline, Inbreeding, Competition, Hybridization, Overfishing added; Habitat destruction / Habitat degradation / Human disturbance consolidated into Habitat loss; final vocabulary = 13 distinct values.
